uxPrinciples: Judge what the visible product proves, not what the implementation intended.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Inbox and message thread pattern
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an inbox/thread structure: sender, timestamp, message preview/body, reply field, invite/block state, and read/received state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material detail surface composition
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

tickets.problemStatement: The evidence does not prove that each workflow/persona UI implements the full production lifecycle. Cards may expose a single accept/cancel action without the decision context, alternate choices, result state, or receiver/continuation state real users need.
tickets.rootCauseHypothesis: The product experience was modeled as completed workflows rather than lifecycle-complete user tasks, so the UI can appear polished while still missing required fields, negative/change actions, and durable post-action states.
tickets.targetExperience: Each workflow/persona surface should show the concrete object, decision information, natural primary and alternate actions, persistent result/receipt/status, and receiver/continuation state expected in a production app.
uxPrinciples: Workflows are product lifecycles, not one-shot checklist actions
Users need enough information to decide before acting
Production affordances include alternate choices, change/revoke paths, and clear result states when the domain requires them
Receiver and continuation states are first-class UX, not hidden backend assertions
concreteImprovements: For every failed lifecycle scorecard, add the missing lifecycle groups named in the ticket.
Update the community product doc workflow section first when the correct lifecycle is ambiguous.
Replace accept/cancel-only cards with product surfaces that include decision data, primary action, alternate/change/reject path, persistent result, and receiver/continuation state.
Recapture entry/action/result/receiver screenshots and rerun the lifecycle judge.
implementationGuidance: Inspect workflow surface builders and identify where current UI collapses lifecycle into a single action card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Inbox and message thread pattern
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an inbox/thread structure: sender, timestamp, message preview/body, reply field, invite/block state, and read/received state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material detail surface composition
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.
